article_title: Should we Tell Teachers That They Are (In)Correct? How Personalized Refutation Text Promotes or Hampers Conceptual Change
citation: Anna-Sophia Dersch · Ian Thacker · Alexander Eitel (2026). Should we Tell Teachers That They Are (In)Correct? How Personalized Refutation Text Promotes or Hampers Conceptual Change. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-026-10116-9
title: Math-gender Misconceptions Questionnaire short version (MGMQ-s)
description: The MGMQ-s is the pre- and post-test measure of teachers' math-gender misconceptions. It "consists of two misconceptions scales (empathizing-systemizing ... and girls' compensation" with four items each, plus eight correct filler items to balance the questionnaire. For each item participants indicate agreement dichotomously and certainty on a five-point Likert scale; misconception scores are computed by multiplying agreement (−1/+1) by certainty (0–4), yielding item values from −4 to +4, with higher scores expressing stronger misconceptions. Items are presented in a newly randomized order per participant.
requirements: A criterion determines a misconception as prevalent if a participant agreed to at least one item per scale with high certainty (certain or absolutely certain)
target_learning_goals: measuring empathizing-systemizing and girls' compensation misconceptions
examples: Used as pre-test and post-test in the 2×2 experiment; conceptual change scores were calculated by subtracting pre-test from post-test results
